title: Reduce SLO alert churn after capacity/regression incident
creator: Ariel Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity regression on 2026-02-27 we experienced a cascade of transient SLO breaches across hosted inference endpoints that produced ~350 alert pages in a 40-minute window. The incident root cause was a regression in autoscaler heuristics (ENG-8200) + an under-tuned paging policy that did not account for multi-tenant bursting patterns. This ticket captures the postmortem action items to reduce alert noise and avoid paging fatigue while preserving timely incident response for true customer-impacting SLO breaches.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ariel Chen: Initial postmortem summary posted to Confluence (see links). Noted that 72% of pages were for transient 1-2 minute error spikes; oncall acknowledged many as false positives.

2026-03-03 - Diego Morales: Drafted change proposal for tiered paging: only page when either (a) >3 customer-facing routes exceed 5% error budget burn for a sustained 10m or (b) total cluster error budget burn >25% over 15m. Uploaded to doc for review.

2026-03-05 - Priya Nandakumar (SRE): Reviewed draft — concerned about delaying pages for multi-region failures. Suggested 'fast-fail' override for region-wide latency SLOs and an emergency pager policy for P0 customers.
2026-03-07 - PM Rafi Gomez: Linked customer impact dashboard; proposed that customer-visible SLOs get lower thresholds (more sensitive) than internal infra SLOs. Agreed to a canary rollout plan.
2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Implemented prometheus rule changes in test cluster (PR #4256) and added dedupe logic in alertmanager. Tests show 60% reduction in pages for simulated transient bursts.
2026-03-12 - Oncall rotation feedback: request for clearer runbook steps on when to escalate to paging, and for a single-panel summary of active SLO burn-rate contributors.
2026-03-14 - Ariel Chen: This ticket split into implementation (this ticket) and follow-up validation (ENG-8230). Tabletop scheduled for 2026-03-18.
Review notes: Design/PM/Eng alignment required on acceptable delays for paging; include product team sign-off before changing customer-facing paging thresholds.
action_items: A1 - Modify paging thresholds: implement tiered paging policy in Alertmanager config. Page only if (i) >3 customer-facing routes breach >5% error budget sustained for >=10m OR (ii) cluster-level error budget burn >25% over 15m. Owner: Diego Morales. Due: 2026-03-14.
A2 - Add transient suppression window: suppress paging for bursts shorter than 3 minutes and produce non-paging incidents instead. Owner: SRE (Priya Nandakumar). Due: 2026-03-16.
A3 - Burn-rate window tuning: introduce adaptive burn-rate windows (1m/5m/15m) and weight by route criticality. Owner: Reliability eng (Diego). Due: 2026-03-18.
A4 - Alert deduplication: add fingerprinting rules in Alertmanager to collapse symptomatically identical alerts across pods into a single page. Owner: Platform infra (Yvonne Park). Due: 2026-03-20.
A5 - Runbook updates: update SLO runbooks to include new paging criteria, decision matrix, and explicit manual-ack escalation rules. Owner: Oncall docs (Samir Patel). Due: 2026-03-17.
A6 - Dashboarding: add an 'SLO burn triage' dashboard that highlights top 10 contributors, per-route burn-rate, and active suppression status. Owner: Observability (Rafi Gomez). Due: 2026-03-15.
A7 - Canary + Rollout: perform a staged rollout (test -> staging -> prod-canary -> prod) and monitor page rates and time-to-detection. Owner: Diego Morales. Due: 2026-03-21.
A8 - Post-deploy validation: run synthetic SLO-breach generator to validate suppression does not mask real degradations. Owner: QA (Nora Li). Due: 2026-03-22.
A9 - Tabletop + training: run a 60-minute tabletop with oncall and PMs to confirm new escalation behavior. Owner: Ariel Chen. Scheduled: 2026-03-18.

A10 - Retro and metrics: track page count, mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), and percentage of pages labeled 'transient' for 8 weeks post-rollout. Owner: Reliability eng. Start date: 2026-03-21.
decisions: D1 - Adopt tiered paging instead of global threshold: balances sensitivity for customer-facing routes with noise reduction for infra-only symptoms.

D2 - Use a 3-minute transient suppression floor: chosen after analyzing 6 months of burst patterns (median transient peak = 72s). Trade-off: small risk of delayed page for short-but-severe failures; mitigated by fast-fail overrides for region-wide signals.
D3 - Implement alert dedupe at Alertmanager level (fingerprinting) rather than downstream oncall client to keep alerting backplane simple.
D4 - Require PM sign-off for any change that increases customer-visible detection delay for SLOs tagged as 'customer-facing'.
D5 - Ship changes behind a config flag and canary route to allow quick rollback if MTTD regresses.

Notes on trade-offs: Longer sustain windows decrease noise but increase time-to-detect; using weighted-criticality keeps high-value customers protected. Decision approved by SRE lead and PM on 2026-03-07.
